hints: Trace the exact journey in order: start in the plasma, then go into and out of the capillary wall cell, then go into and out of the alveolar wall cell to reach the air space.
Remember every whole cell you go through means two membrane crossings, one to get in and one to get out. How many whole cells are in this route?
walkthrough:
**Picture the journey**

Great, let us walk with the CO2 molecule. It starts free in the plasma of the blood. To get to the air in the alveolus it must pass through two layers of cells: the endothelial cell of the capillary wall and then the epithelial cell of the alveolus wall.

**Count two crossings per cell**

This is the key rule. A cell surface membrane surrounds the cell, so going right through a cell always means 2 crossings. One to enter the cytoplasm, and one to leave it.

**Add them up to reach the alveolus**

Into capillary endothelial cell = 1, out of it = 2. Then into alveolar epithelial cell = 3, out of it into the alveolar air space = 4. So the total is 4 crossings.

options.A: 1 is too few. It counts only one entry and forgets that the molecule must also leave each cell and then cross a second cell.
options.B: 2 would be correct for passing through just one cell, but here the CO2 must pass through both the capillary cell and the alveolar cell.
options.C: 3 misses one crossing. You cannot have an odd number when you go completely through two cells, each needs an in and an out.
options.D: 4 is correct: 2 crossings for the capillary wall cell plus 2 crossings for the alveolar wall cell to enter the alveolus.
